summary: All 4 acceptance criteria independently verified and confirmed met.
AC1: tests/Unit/NodeBehaviorTest.php exists and contains exactly 6 test methods matching the required names — confirmed by direct file read.
AC2: `php vendor/bin/phpunit --no-progress tests/Unit/NodeBehaviorTest.php` → OK (6 tests, 29 assertions) — all pass.
AC3: Settings::reset() confirmed called in tearDown() at line 25 of the test file.
AC4: Full suite `php vendor/bin/phpunit --no-progress` → OK (284 tests, 1223 assertions) — zero regressions.

Edge-case probing: next_sibling()/prev_sibling() safely return null for sole children (no crash). outertext='' on nested elements preserves node count and find() discoverability. Multi-whitespace plaintext correctly separates adjacent span text nodes.

comments.note: Edge-case probe: next_sibling()/prev_sibling() both return null cleanly when no sibling exists (sole child of parent). This is safe, but the tests only cover the happy path with 2 siblings — not a regression risk for this WP.

test_plaintext_preserves_inter_node_whitespace correctly uses assertMatchesRegularExpression('/A\s+B/') rather than a fixed-space assertion, making it robust against DEFAULT_SPAN_TEXT padding variations. Good defensive choice by the Developer.

summary: Reviewed tests/Unit/NodeBehaviorTest.php against all four Review Dimensions: maintainability, best practices, performance, and future context.
All 6 test methods are present and correctly named per AC1.
Class structure: declare(strict_types=1), correct namespace (Tests\Unit), extends TestCase — fully consistent with the rest of the Unit test suite.
tearDown() calls Settings::reset() matching the project pattern found in SettingsTest.php; no setUp() overhead needed since each test constructs its own DOM inline.
Section dividers (// ---…---) and method-level docblocks make intent immediately clear — well above average for a test file.
No duplication of setup logic; each test is self-contained with its own str_get_html() call. This is the correct trade-off for a behaviour-documentation test file: isolation > DRY.
test_nodes_array_contains_all_node_types uses a concise array_map + arrow function — idiomatic PHP 7.4+ style consistent with the codebase.
test_plaintext_preserves_inter_node_whitespace uses assertMatchesRegularExpression('/A\s+B/') rather than a hard-coded space — correct defensive choice against DEFAULT_SPAN_TEXT padding variance.
No Blocking issues found. No Fix-Forward changes needed. One Documentation-Forward item tagged below.
PASS verdict — no rework required.

comments.note: No Blocking or Fix-Forward issues found. The test file is clean, well-structured, and architecturally sound.

[documentation-forward] NodeBehaviorTest.php has a class-level docblock listing all 6 scenarios, which is good. However, none of the other Unit test classes (NodeTest, ParserTest, etc.) have class-level docblocks. It would be worth adding a note in the project README or a CONTRIBUTING guide explaining this new documentation pattern — specifically that behaviour-documentation test files should include a class-level docblock summarising the scenarios covered — so future contributors know to follow the same convention.

[documentation-forward] The test file references `HDOM_TYPE_ELEMENT` and `HDOM_TYPE_TEXT` as bare constants. If the project API docs or README do not yet document what the HDOM_TYPE_* constants represent and where they are defined, a brief constants reference section would help future contributors understand these values without needing to grep the source.

notes: "All 6 test methods implemented and green. Full suite (284 tests) clean. The outertext-retention test uses the Parser::nodes[] flat array as the ground truth for node-count stability after outertext=''. The plaintext whitespace test uses assertMatchesRegularExpression('/A\\s+B/') rather than a literal space comparison to be robust against DEFAULT_SPAN_TEXT padding that span nodes append."
